notes:
A speech balloon is now said in one breath.

The text reader hands back a bubble either whole or split into its printed lines, and nothing about the page says which. When it split, the voice read each piece as its own sentence — "Could you." "Calmly explain to me." "What happened?" — for a bubble that reads "Could you calmly explain to me what happened?". The words were right and it still sounded broken. A bubble's lines are put back together now.

On the page this was measured against, three chopped-up bubbles became whole sentences.

Preparing a chapter can also be stopped now, and picks up where it left off — a long chapter is several minutes of work and there was no way out of it.
